# Translation of the Sumerian Text

1. In those distant days, when heaven and earth had been fashioned together,
2. In those distant nights, when heaven and earth had been fashioned together,
3. In those distant years, when destinies had been decreed,
4. When the Anunna gods had been born,
5. When the divine spouses had been taken in marriage,
6. When the divine spouses had been distributed throughout heaven and earth,
7. When the divine spouses had become pregnant and given birth,
8. When the gods, for their food rations, were bound to their … dining halls,
9. The myriad gods stood at the labor, the lesser gods bore the drudgery,
10. The gods were dredging the canals, they were heaping up their silt in Ḫarali,
11. The gods, grinding away, were complaining about their lives.
12. At that time, the one of broad wisdom, the creator of the myriad gods,
13. Enki, in the deep Engur, in the flowing waters, a place into whose interior no god could gaze,
14. Was lying on his bed and would not rise from his sleep.
15. The gods were weeping, saying "It is he who has caused the lamentation!"
16. To the one who lay sleeping, to the one who would not rise from his bed,
17. Namma, the primordial mother who gave birth to the myriad gods,
18. Brought the tears of the gods before her son:
19. "Is he really lying there? Is he really sleeping,
20. And … will not rise?
21. The gods, your handiwork, are smiting their … necks!

(This is the opening of *Enki and Ninmaḫ*, the Sumerian myth describing the creation of humankind, in which the gods complain about their toil and Namma rouses Enki to fashion mortals to relieve them of their labor.)
